# Triton Control

> Operate NVIDIA Triton Inference Server on Kubernetes from one open-source control plane.

Triton Control is an open-source web application for managing NVIDIA Triton
Inference Server environments. It combines deployment workflows, model
repositories, inference testing, performance analysis, development workspaces,
MLflow, Argo Workflows, S3 integration, and user access control in one UI.

The primary deployment target is Kubernetes through the Helm chart in
`charts/triton-control`. The application can also run with Docker Compose,
Podman Compose, or separate Python and npm processes for local development.

## Docs

- [Documentation](https://ai-lab-tech.github.io/triton-control/): Project documentation home.
- [Getting Started](https://ai-lab-tech.github.io/triton-control/getting-started/): Kubernetes, Docker Compose, Podman Compose, and local development setup.
- [User Guide](https://ai-lab-tech.github.io/triton-control/user-guide/): Dashboard, instances, inference, S3, deployments, Perf Analyzer, MLflow, and user workflows.
- [Deployment](https://ai-lab-tech.github.io/triton-control/deployment/): Kubernetes prerequisites, Helm deployment, Docker Compose, and Podman Compose.
- [Configuration](https://ai-lab-tech.github.io/triton-control/configuration/): Backend environment variables, OIDC modes, and GitOps examples.
- [API](https://ai-lab-tech.github.io/triton-control/api/): OpenAPI, Swagger, ReDoc, and frontend client generation.

## Source

- [README](README.md): Project overview, core capabilities, and run instructions.
- [Backend](triton-backend/): Python FastAPI backend.
- [Frontend](triton-frontend/): Angular Material frontend.
- [Helm chart](charts/triton-control/): Kubernetes deployment chart.
- [Examples](examples/): Example model repositories and deployment assets.
- [Development docs](docs/development.md): Local development workflow, tests, and CI checks.

## Notes For AI Assistants

- Prefer the checked-in documentation under `docs/` for project behavior and
  operating guidance.
- Regenerate and commit OpenAPI artifacts when backend request or response
  schemas change.
- Keep Kubernetes-specific behavior aligned with the Helm chart and backend
  in-cluster detection logic.
